measures.officialStatement:
IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS OF MEASURE S
By Dawyn R. Harrison, County Counsel
This measure was placed on the ballot by the governing board (Board) of the Charter Oak Unified School District (District). If approved by at least 55 percent of the votes cast on the measure, this measure will authorize the District to issue and sell up to $75,000,000 in general obligation bonds. The sale of these bonds by the District represents a debt of the District.
Proceeds from the sale of bonds authorized by this measure may only be used by the District for the acquisition, construction, reconstruction, rehabilitation or replacement of school facilities, including the furnishing and equipping of school facilities. A complete list of the projects and allowed expenditures is included in the full text of the measure. Bond proceeds may not be used for teacher and administrator salaries and other operating expenses.
If the measure is approved, the Board will be required to establish an independent Citizens' Oversight Committee and have independent performance and financial audits conducted annually to ensure that bond proceeds are spent only for projects identified in the measure. The District will deposit bond proceeds into a separate account and comply with the reporting requirements of the Government Code.
According to the District's Tax Rate Statement, the best estimate of the average annual tax rate required to fund the bonds is $40.00 per $100,000 of assessed value. The best estimate of the highest tax rate required to fund the bonds is $40.00 per $100,000 of assessed value. The final fiscal year in which the tax is anticipated to be collected is fiscal year 2061-62. The best estimate of the total debt service, including principal and interest, required to be repaid if all bonds are issued and sold is approximately $157,000,000. The bonds will not exceed the maximum interest rate as allowed by law.

measures.officialStatement:
IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS OF MEASURE SMS
By Dawyn R. Harrison, County Counsel
This measure was placed on the ballot by the governing board (Board) of the San Marino Unified School District (District). If approved by two-thirds (2/3) of the votes cast on the measure, this measure would authorize the District to combine and extend two existing special parcel taxes, known as Measure E and Measure R, into one special parcel tax of $1,499 per parcel of taxable real property (Tax).
If approved, the Tax will be levied annually for six years, beginning July 1, 2027, and ending June 30, 2033. Beginning July 1, 2028, the Tax would increase each year by a cost-of-living adjustment equal to the lesser of three percent or the annual average percentage change in the Los Angeles Metropolitan Statistical Area Consumer Price Index.
The measure defines a "Parcel of Taxable Real Property" (Parcel) as any parcel of land that lies wholly or partially within the District and that receives a separate tax bill for ad valorem property taxes from the Los Angeles County Treasurer and Tax Collector (County Tax Collector). Parcels that are otherwise exempt from ad valorem property taxes in any year would also be exempt from the Tax. Certain contiguous parcels under identical ownership and used solely for owner-occupied, single-family residential purposes may be treated as a single parcel under District procedures. The Tax would be collected by the County Tax Collector, with unpaid taxes to bear interest at the same rate applicable to unpaid ad valorem property taxes.
As stated in the full text of the Measure, proceeds from the Tax shall be used only for specified purposes, including to:
- Retain and attract the best qualified teachers and counselors and ensure the continuation of teaching positions;
- Maintain existing educational programs at current levels;
- Maintain class size;
- Maintain district-wide school library media specialists; and
- Maintain and fund technology systems and personnel, as well as academic and college counseling positions.
Tax proceeds must be deposited into a separate account, with an annual written report to be prepared by the District detailing the collection and expenditure of the proceeds.
If this measure is approved, the existing Measure R tax of $415 per year would no longer be collected on or after July 1, 2027. If this measure is not approved, the Measure R tax will continue to be collected until June 30, 2031. This measure would not affect the existing Measure E tax, which is scheduled to continue at $1,084 per parcel through June 30, 2027.
An exemption may be applied for with the District on any Parcel owned by one or more persons who occupy such parcel as their principal residence and are: (1) 65 years of age or older on or before to June 30 of the preceding fiscal year; (2) receives Supplemental Security Income for a disability regardless of age; or (3) receives Social Security Disability Insurance benefits regardless of age and whose yearly income does not exceed 250 percent of the 2012 federal poverty guidelines. Exemptions granted under prior qualified special taxes will not require re-approval. The District's decisions regarding the Tax, including exemptions, would be final and binding.

measures.officialStatement:
IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS OF MEASURE LV
By Dawyn R. Harrison, County Counsel
This measure was placed on the ballot by the governing board (Board) of the Las Virgenes Unified School District (District). If approved by two-thirds (2/3) of the votes cast on the measure, this measure would authorize the District to raise additional revenue by levying a special parcel tax of $98 per parcel (Tax). If approved, the Tax will be levied annually for twelve years, beginning July 1, 2028. This Tax would extend an existing special parcel tax of $98 per parcel per year that is due to expire on June 30, 2028.
The measure defines "Parcel" (Parcel) as any parcel of land that lies wholly or partially within the District and that receives a separate tax bill for ad valorem property taxes from the Los Angeles County Treasurer and Tax Collector or the Ventura County Treasurer-Tax Collector (collectively, Tax Collector). Parcels that are otherwise exempt from ad valorem property taxes in any year would also be exempt from the Tax. Certain contiguous parcels under identical ownership and used solely for owner-occupied, single-family residential purposes may be treated as a single parcel under District procedures. The Tax would be collected by the applicable Tax Collector, with unpaid taxes to bear interest at the same rate applicable to unpaid ad valorem property taxes.
Proceeds from the Tax shall be used only for purposes specified in the Measure, including to:
- Continue offering core academic programs in math, science and technology;
- Continue funding for core programs in reading and the arts and funding for athletics;
- Maintain class sizes;
- Keep textbooks, technology, and instructional materials up-to-date; and
- Attract and retain highly qualified teachers, counselors, career advisors, and technology specialists.
Tax proceeds cannot be used for administrator salaries, benefits, or pensions. Tax proceeds must be deposited into a separate account, with a Citizens' Oversight Committee to provide oversight as to the expenditure of the proceeds. The chief fiscal officer of the District will also prepare an annual written report detailing the collection and expenditure of the proceeds.
An exemption may be applied for with the District on any Parcel owned by one or more persons who occupy such Parcel as their principal residence and is/are: (1) 65 years of age or older on or before to June 30 of the preceding fiscal year; (2) receives Supplemental Security Income for a disability regardless of age; or (3) receives Social Security Disability Insurance benefits regardless of age and whose yearly income does not exceed 250 percent of the 2012 federal poverty guidelines. Persons currently exempted from the District's expiring special parcel tax will remain exempt and not be required to reapply for exemption. The District's decisions regarding the Tax, including exemptions, would be final and binding.

This measure was placed on the ballot by the governing board (Board) of the Bellflower Unified School District (District). If approved by at least 55 percent of the votes cast on the measure, this measure will authorize the District to issue and sell up to $135,000,000 in general obligation bonds. The sale of these bonds by the District represents a debt of the District.
Proceeds from the sale of bonds authorized by this measure may only be used by the District for the construction, reconstruction, rehabilitation, replacement, furnishing and equipping of school facilities, or the acquisition or lease of real property for school facilities. A complete list of the projects and allowed expenditures is included in the full text of the measure. Bond proceeds may not be used for teacher and administrator salaries and other operating expenses.
If the measure is approved, the Board will be required to establish an independent Citizens' Oversight Committee and have independent performance and financial audits conducted annually to ensure that bond proceeds are spent only for projects identified in the measure. The Board will deposit bond proceeds into a separate account. Approval of the measure does not guarantee that projects described in the measure will be funded beyond local revenues generated by the measure. The District's proposal for certain projects may assume receipt of matching State funds subject to appropriation by the Legislature or approval of a statewide bond measure.
According to the District's Tax Rate Statement, the best estimate of the average annual tax rate required to fund the bonds is $45.78 per $100,000 of assessed value. The best estimate of the highest tax rate required to fund the bonds is $49.00 per $100,000 of assessed value. The final fiscal year in which the tax is anticipated to be collected is fiscal year 2057-58. The best estimate of the total debt service, including principal and interest, required to be repaid if all bonds are issued and sold is $240,900,000. The bonds will not exceed the maximum interest rate as allowed by law.

measures.officialStatement:
IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS OF MEASURE B
By Dawyn R. Harrison, County Counsel
This measure was placed on the ballot by the governing board (Board) of the Hacienda La Puente Unified School District (District). If approved by a majority of the votes cast on the measure, this measure will establish a limit on the number of terms an elected Board member may serve to two (2) full four-year terms during their lifetime.
There is currently no limit on the number of terms that an elected member may serve on the Board. This measure establishes a limit on the maximum number of terms an elected member may serve on the Board to two (2) full four-year terms during that elected member's lifetime, regardless of the trustee area represented.
If approved, this measure will apply prospectively and any full four-year term served on or after November 3, 2026 will count toward the term limit.
NO ARGUMENT FOR OR AGAINST THIS MEASURE WAS SUBMITTED

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Combine and renew San Marino Unified’s two existing school parcel taxes at their current combined rate of $1,499 per taxable parcel each year for six years, July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2033. From July 1, 2028, the annual adjustment would equal the lesser of 3% or the specified consumer-price-index change; the board could choose a lower adjustment. Estimated annual revenue is $6.1 million, restricted to the listed educational programs, teachers, counselors, class sizes, libraries and technology. Money must go into a separate fund, with annual collection and spending reports. Existing and new senior/disability exemptions and parcel-combination rules are described below. The measure would replace the $415 Measure R tax from July 2027; the $1,084 Measure E tax is already scheduled to expire that June. Approval requires two-thirds of votes.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the combined six-year parcel tax and its annual adjustment, restricted uses and exemption rules.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve the combined renewal. Measure E would expire June 30, 2027, while the existing $415 Measure R tax would continue through June 30, 2031.

parts.label: Senior and disability exemptions
parts.what: Owner-occupants may apply under district procedures if age 65 or older before June 30 of the preceding fiscal year, receiving Supplemental Security Income for disability at any age, or receiving Social Security Disability Insurance with annual income no greater than 250% of the 2012 federal poverty guidelines. Prior exemptions would continue without a new application, subject to verification of ongoing eligibility.

parts.label: What counts as a parcel
parts.what: A separately billed parcel wholly or partly in the district is taxable. Property exempt from regular property taxes remains exempt. Contiguous parcels with identical ownership used solely as an owner-occupied single-family home may be treated as one parcel under district procedures. If that definition is legally invalid, the fallback is each assessor-numbered parcel in the district, which could increase the number taxed.

parts.label: Inflation, reports and other funding
parts.what: The adjustment uses the Los Angeles metropolitan consumer-price index for the prior 12 months as of December 1; CPI-U is the fallback if that index is unavailable. The board could lower the adjustment when sufficient or appropriate, including in response to state-budget changes. The district’s spending limit would adjust by tax collections. Annual reports are due by December 31. The board could reduce the tax if needed to restore government funding affected by the local tax or improve the district’s fiscal position.
